findings.description: plans/ralph-pipeline-04-pipeline-overview.md line 31 documents `scoreRecommendations(byTaskId, overviewData) -> Recommendation[]` as a positional-argument function, but the shipped implementation in scripts/lib/score-recommendations.mjs:25 exports `scoreRecommendations({ byTaskId, overviewData, prdsByTaskId, config } = {})` — a single options object with a required `prdsByTaskId` carrier and an optional `config`. plans/ralph-pipeline-INDEX.md line 200 already documents the correct shape, so the plan is the only outlier and will mislead any future reader who tries to call the function from the plan signature.
findings.suggestedFix: Update plans/ralph-pipeline-04-pipeline-overview.md line 31 (and the matching `Inputs:` line ~48) to: `pure function scoreRecommendations({ byTaskId, overviewData, prdsByTaskId, config? }) -> Recommendation[]`. Mention that `prdsByTaskId` is required and is carried as a non-enumerable property on the state object via `getPrdsByTaskId(state)`.

findings.description: plans/ralph-pipeline-04-pipeline-overview.md line 56 documents `deriveDependencyGraph(overviewData)` as a single-positional-arg call, but the shipped implementation in scripts/lib/derive-dependency-graph.mjs:1 exports `deriveDependencyGraph({ generatedAt, generatedFromCommit, overviewData, byTaskId, prdsByTaskId } = {})`. The plan signature is missing `generatedAt`, `generatedFromCommit`, `byTaskId`, and `prdsByTaskId`. INDEX line 201 already documents the correct shape.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace line 56 with: `Call deriveDependencyGraph({ generatedAt, generatedFromCommit, overviewData, byTaskId, prdsByTaskId }) → write plans/overview-dependency-graph.json atomically.` Note in the surrounding text that story node IDs are namespaced as `${taskId}:${storyId}` and edges use `source`/`target` rather than `from`/`to`.

findings.description: plans/ralph-pipeline-04-pipeline-overview.md lines 54-57 describe sidecar emission happening `after mergeAndWrite produces the new sidecar state`, but the shipped implementation in scripts/lib/sync-core.mjs:320-348 calls `emitDerivedArtifacts(...)` from inside `writeSidecar({ repoRoot, config, state })` (line 348), which is reached by BOTH the one-shot CLI path and the watcher cold-start path. The job CLAUDE.md explicitly warns that `Hooking only mergeAndWrite silently breaks the one-shot path` — the plan text contradicts the as-built emission contract and could regress future refactors.
findings.suggestedFix: Rewrite the bullets under `To modify > scripts/lib/sync-core.mjs` to say: `writeSidecar({ repoRoot, config, state }) emits plans/overview-recommendations.json and plans/overview-dependency-graph.json via emitDerivedArtifacts({ repoRoot, config, recommendations, dependencyGraph }) after the sidecar .js/.json writes are durable. mergeAndWrite reaches the same emission by calling writeSidecar; the one-shot CLI path and watcher cold-start both call writeSidecar directly and therefore also fire emitDerivedArtifacts.` Also call out that `atomicWriteFile` is exported from sync-core.mjs for reuse.

findings.description: plans/ralph-pipeline-04-pipeline-overview.md line 118 (Verification step C) instructs the reviewer to run `cat plans/overview-recommendations.json | jq '.recommendations[0:5]'`, but the shipped artifact is a bare `Recommendation[]` array (confirmed: the file starts with `[` and contains no top-level `recommendations` key). The verification command will return `null` against the real artifact and falsely fail the AC. plans/ralph-pipeline-04-refresh-changelog.md line 8 already documents this exact normalization for Plan 06.
findings.suggestedFix: Change line 118 to: `cat plans/overview-recommendations.json | jq '.[0:5]'` and add a note that the file is a bare ranked `Recommendation[]` array (not a wrapper object), matching INDEX line 200 and the Plan 05 / Plan 06 / Plan 09 consumers.

findings.description: plans/ralph-pipeline-04-pipeline-overview.md line 47 specifies the `PipelineOverview` empty state should render literally `No Ralph state tracked yet — run pnpm sync-ralph-state or check unmatched in stderr`, but the shipped component at tools/overview-viewer/src/components/PipelineOverview.tsx:29 renders `No Ralph stage data` and the interaction test at tools/overview-viewer/src/__tests__/interactions/pipelineOverview.test.tsx:94,97 asserts that exact shorter string. A reader following the plan will misimplement the empty state and the existing test will fail.
findings.suggestedFix:
Update line 47 to reflect the as-built empty-state copy: `Empty state: when ralphState is null OR total count is 0, render
No Ralph stage data
.` Optionally add a one-line note explaining why the shorter copy was chosen (asserted verbatim by the interactions test) so a future refactor doesn't reintroduce the longer string and break the test.

findings.description: plans/ralph-pipeline-04-pipeline-overview.md line 33 says `Scoring weights override lives in the main .ralph/overview-config.json under a recommendations.weights key (default 40/30/20/10 from the comprehensive plan)`. The shipped config schema (`.ralph/overview-config.schema.json`) and defaults add a full `recommendations` block (`topN` + `weights`) AND new `outputs.recommendationsJson` and `outputs.dependencyGraphJson` path keys, both of which the job CLAUDE.md (lines 17-18) lists as mandatory closed-schema additions. The plan never mentions `topN` or the new output paths, leaving the schema surface under-documented.
findings.suggestedFix: Extend line 33 to enumerate the four new closed-schema keys: `outputs.recommendationsJson`, `outputs.dependencyGraphJson`, `recommendations.topN`, and `recommendations.weights` (with the 40/30/20/10 defaults). Note that the schema is closed (additionalProperties: false) and additions must touch `.ralph/overview-config.schema.json`, `scripts/lib/default-config.mjs`, `scripts/lib/default-config.d.mts`, and `scripts/lib/resolve-config.mjs` in lockstep.
